# Memory and Latent World Models\chaptersubtitle{Spatial Frame Trees, Persistence, and Uncertainty Expansion}

![Systems Organ Focus: Stage 3 (World Models, Latent Predictive Dynamics, and Spatial $SE(3)$ State).](figures/fig_pipeline_locator.svg){#fig-locator-ch05 width=100% fig-pos="H"}

*Why does an autonomous manipulator crush a workpiece the instant its own mechanical arm blocks its camera view?*

In digital simulation, the physical state of every entity is permanently accessible in global memory arrays. In the physical world, sensory contact is intermittent: objects pass behind occlusions, sensors suffer dropouts, and cameras are blinded by the robot's own moving linkages. An embodied agent cannot rely solely on instantaneous sensory snapshots, nor can it afford the computational cost of generating raw video pixels in real time. Instead, it must maintain a structured, latent representation of physical reality—anchored by time-indexed coordinate frame trees in $SE(3)$, forward predictive dynamics in compact latent space, and expanding spatial uncertainty envelopes that mathematically enforce when memory expires.

{{< pagebreak >}}

::: {.callout-objective}
By the conclusion of this chapter, you will be able to:

1. **Contrast Generative vs. Latent World Modeling:** Explain why real-time pixel generation (video diffusion) fails on compute and hallucination budgets, and deploy non-generative Latent World Models (JEPAs, RSSMs) that predict transitions in compact representation space $\mathcal{Z}$.
2. **Maintain Dynamic Metric $SE(3)$ Transform Graphs:** Construct and query time-indexed Lie group coordinate frame trees ($\mathcal{T}_{\text{frames}}$) using Lie algebra ($\mathfrak{se}(3)$) tangent-space integration to eliminate gimbal lock and timestamp skew.
3. **Formulate Spatial Persistence Under Occlusion:** Model object permanence across visual dropouts using forward kinematic prediction and stochastic state propagation.
4. **Quantify Spatial Uncertainty Expansion & Expiration:** Formulate positional covariance growth ($\sigma_{\text{pos}}(t) = \sigma_0 + v_{\text{target}} \cdot \Delta t$) and enforce hard Time-To-Live (TTL) state leases.
5. **Architect Memory Domain Isolation:** Decouple high-bandwidth, non-deterministic latent belief updates (Linux MPU) from deterministic, high-rate proprioceptive state estimation (Real-Time MCU).
6. **Freeze the State and Timing Model:** Author the fifth artifact of the engineering notebook establishing coordinate hierarchies, TTL windows, covariance bounds, and thermal derating regimes.

**Core Chapter Takeaway:** Observation is not state; because physical contact is intermittent and occlusions are inevitable, an embodied agent must sustain a persistent coordinate frame tree and model spatial uncertainty growth to survive sensory blackouts.
:::

## The Persistence Imperative: Why Observation Is Not State

In digital computer science, memory is an infinite, addressable grid of bytes. In modern machine learning, memory is often conceptualized as the attention context window of a transformer: a static sequence of tokens cached in GPU high-bandwidth memory. If an object is described in token 42, the model attends to it with mathematical permanence. When the text stream ends or the context window shifts, the digital entity simply ceases to exist.

The physical world is neither stateless nor an infinite text buffer. In the physical world, matter possesses mass, momentum, and continuous geometry ($W_t \to W_{t+1}$). When a robotic manipulator reaches toward a component on an assembly bench, the robot's own mechanical wrist inevitably passes between the overhead camera and the target object. For a span of $150\text{ to }300\text{ milliseconds}$, optical photons from the target cannot reach the camera sensor. The target object has vanished from the camera's field of view.

A naive perception system operating in a purely reactive loop suffers an immediate cognitive collapse:

$$\begin{aligned}
\text{Reactive Vision: } &\text{Photons Blocked} \implies \text{Zero Detections} \implies \text{Pose Lost} \\
\text{Physical Reality: } &\text{Matter Persists } (T_{\text{target}}^{\text{world}} \in SE(3)) \implies \text{Uncertainty Expands } (\sigma \propto \Delta t)
\end{aligned}$$

The physical object did not dissolve into non-existence simply because a camera lens was occluded. It still occupies space, possesses inertia, and presents a rigid physical boundary. However, because the agent can no longer observe it directly, the agent's internal certainty regarding the object's precise coordinates begins to decay. If the object is resting on a stationary workbench, its coordinates remain fixed, but mechanical vibration and base drift introduce positional doubt. If the object is carried on a moving conveyor belt, its position drifts rapidly according to the belt's velocity vector.

To act competently in an un-instrumented physical world, an embodied agent cannot rely on instantaneous pixel reactions alone. It must construct and maintain a continuous, metric latent world model and temporal state belief ($S(t)$). This internal state organ performs three load-bearing systems tasks: temporal synchronization across disparate sensor rates, spatial metric persistence in $SE(3)$, and bounded uncertainty tracking with state expiration leases.

## Kinematic Coordinate Frame Trees and Uncertainty Propagation

Parallel to latent neural features, an embodied agent maintains metric spatial coordinate frames across its physical linkages and environmental fixtures. The rigid spatial transform between coordinate frame $A$ and frame $B$ is a member of the Special Euclidean Group $SE(3)$ [@murray2017mathematical; @lynch2017modern]:

$$\mathbf{T}_B^A = \begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{R}_B^A & \mathbf{p}_B^A \\ \mathbf{0}^T & 1 \end{bmatrix} \in SE(3), \quad \mathbf{R} \in SO(3), \; \mathbf{p} \in \mathbb{R}^3$$

Representing rotations with Euler angles induces mathematical singularities (gimbal lock). Physical AI architectures represent spatial transformations using the Lie group $SE(3)$ and perform continuous kinematic integration in the Lie algebra tangent space $\mathfrak{se}(3)$:

$$\boldsymbol{\xi} = \begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{v} \\ \boldsymbol{\omega} \end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^6, \qquad \boldsymbol{\xi}^\wedge = \begin{bmatrix} \boldsymbol{\omega}^\wedge & \mathbf{v} \\ \mathbf{0}^T & 0 \end{bmatrix} \in \mathfrak{se}(3)$$

The matrix exponential maps tangent-space velocity twists directly onto smooth rigid-body motions:

$$\mathbf{T}(t + \Delta t) = \mathbf{T}(t) \cdot \exp\left( \boldsymbol{\xi}^\wedge \Delta t \right)$$

These transformations form an $SE(3)$ frame tree ($\mathcal{T}_{\text{frames}}$), managed via lock-free circular ring buffers that store time-stamped transforms $\mathbf{T}_i(t_i)$. When a high-level query requests the pose of the end-effector at historical time $t_{\text{query}}$ (matching a delayed camera exposure midpoint), the transform buffer performs geodesic interpolation on the Lie group $SE(3)$:

$$\mathbf{T}(t_{\text{query}}) = \mathbf{T}_1 \cdot \exp\left( \alpha \cdot \log\left( \mathbf{T}_1^{-1} \mathbf{T}_2 \right) \right), \quad \alpha = \frac{t_{\text{query}} - t_1}{t_2 - t_1}$$

During visual occlusions, the physical universe does not freeze. Moving objects coast along inertial trajectories, while static obstacles drift in relative coordinates due to platform motion. When direct sensory contact is lost at time $t_0$, the spatial uncertainty envelope grows monotonically with elapsed time $\Delta t = t - t_0$:

$$\sigma_{\text{pos}}(\Delta t) = \sigma_0 + v_{\text{drift}} \cdot \Delta t + \frac{1}{2} a_{\text{max}} \cdot (\Delta t)^2$$

Where $\sigma_0$ is the initial sensor calibration covariance. Given an allowable obstacle clearance $d_{\text{clearance}}$ and a safety margin $d_{\text{margin}}$, setting $\sigma_{\text{pos}}(t_{\text{max}}) = d_{\text{clearance}} - d_{\text{margin}}$ defines the **Maximum Occlusion Horizon ($t_{\text{max}}$)**:

$$t_{\text{max}} = \frac{d_{\text{clearance}} - d_{\text{margin}} - \sigma_0}{v_{\text{drift}}}$$

Beyond $t_{\text{max}}$, spatial uncertainty exceeds available clearance, and candidate proposals become active collision hazards.

### Innovation Residuals and Sensor Fault Gating

When a new measurement $\mathbf{z}_t$ arrives, the state estimator computes the normalized Mahalanobis distance $d_M$ across the innovation covariance $\mathbf{S}_t = \mathbf{H}_t \mathbf{P}_t \mathbf{H}_t^T + \mathbf{R}_t$:

$$d_M = \sqrt{\mathbf{y}_t^T \mathbf{S}_t^{-1} \mathbf{y}_t}, \quad \mathbf{y}_t = \mathbf{z}_t - h(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_t)$$

Physical AI systems enforce a strict $3\sigma$ Innovation Gating Rule: accept if $d_M \le 3.0$; veto if $d_M > 3.0$. A sudden innovation residual spike detects false-positive perception, mechanical tooling jams, or deformed camera mounting brackets.

### Proprioceptive Interoception: 3-Zone Thermal Derating

Motor stator winding temperature rise follows:

$$C_{\text{th}} \frac{d(\Delta T)}{dt} = I^2(t) R(T) - \frac{\Delta T(t)}{R_{\text{th}}}$$

To prevent winding enamel breakdown ($>155^\circ\text{C}$), the state model enforces a continuous 3-Zone Thermal Derating Law (@tbl-thermal-derating):

$$\tau_{\text{max}}(T_{\text{motor}}) = \begin{cases} \tau_{\text{nom}} & \text{if } T_{\text{motor}} < 85^\circ\text{C} \\ \tau_{\text{nom}} \cdot \left(1 - \frac{T_{\text{motor}} - 85^\circ\text{C}}{105^\circ\text{C} - 85^\circ\text{C}}\right) & \text{if } 85^\circ\text{C} \le T_{\text{motor}} \le 105^\circ\text{C} \\ 0\text{ Nm} \quad (\text{Hardware PWM Disconnect}) & \text{if } T_{\text{motor}} > 105^\circ\text{C} \end{cases}$$

| Operating Thermal Zone | Winding Temperature Range ($T_{\text{motor}}$) | Permissible Actuator Torque ($\tau_{\text{max}}$) | Systems Action & Reflex State |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **1. Nominal Operating Zone** | $T_{\text{motor}} < 85^\circ\text{C}$ | $100\%$ Rated Continuous Torque | Full autonomous capability; high-speed trajectory proposals permitted. |
| **2. Linear Derating Zone** | $85^\circ\text{C} \le T_{\text{motor}} \le 105^\circ\text{C}$ | Linearly derated from $100\%$ down to $0\%$ | MPU motion planner scales down maximum acceleration; fan cooling forced to $100\%$. |
| **3. Thermal Emergency Cutoff** | $T_{\text{motor}} > 105^\circ\text{C}$ | $0\text{ Nm}$ (Inverter tri-state disconnect) | **Hardware Reflex:** Disables PWM gate drivers to prevent permanent winding demagnetization. |

: Actuator Thermal Derating Ledger. Dynamic torque throttling regimes as motor winding temperatures approach physical insulation limits. {#tbl-thermal-derating}

## Latent Predictive World Models and Silicon State Memory

When machine learning researchers consider world modeling, the prevailing paradigm is often generative: predicting future video frames pixel-by-pixel using diffusion models or autoregressive video transformers [@ho2020denoising; @singer2022make; @brohan2023rt2].

In embodied Physical AI, predicting future sensory observations at the raw pixel level is an architectural trap governed by three severe physical constraints:

1. **The FLOP and Bandwidth Tax:** Generating uncompressed video frames ($1080\text{p} \times 30\text{ FPS}$) requires tens of trillions of floating-point operations per second (TFLOPS) and floods shared DRAM crossbars, inflating inference latency well past the physical world deadline ($\tau_{\text{world}}$).
2. **The Visual Hallucination Tax:** Autoregressive pixel decoders hallucinate fine high-frequency visual textures. An autonomous vehicle cannot tolerate a generative model that hallucinates or erases an obstacle boundary across consecutive diffusion steps.
3. **The Lack of Metric Geometry:** Video pixels carry no intrinsic metric scale. A downstream trajectory planner cannot compute motor torques from RGB bitmaps; it requires Euclidean coordinates and surface normals in meters and radians.

### Latent Representations and JEPAs

To achieve real-time predictive world modeling, Physical AI discards pixel generation in favor of **Latent World Models** that predict state transitions entirely within compact representation spaces ($z_t \in \mathbb{R}^d$):

**Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA / V-JEPA):** JEPAs [@lecun2022path; @assran2023self] map sensory observations $o_t$ into latent embeddings $\mathbf{z}_t \in \mathcal{Z}$. Instead of reconstructing pixels, the predictor forecasts future latent state $\mathbf{z}_{t+1}$ given proposed action $a_t$:
$$\hat{\mathbf{z}}_{t+1} = g_\theta(\mathbf{z}_t, a_t)$$

JEPAs utilize a Context encoder to process visible observations, and a Target encoder (updated via exponential moving average, EMA) to produce stable representation targets for masked or future regions. By discarding non-predictable visual noise (such as flickering shadows and grass texture) and focusing exclusively on invariant geometric structure and physics, JEPAs execute forward predictions in under $5\text{ ms}$ on edge NPUs.

### Recurrent State-Space Models (RSSMs)

**Recurrent State-Space Models (RSSM):** RSSMs [@hafner2019dreamer; @hafner2023mastering] maintain a dual latent state combining a deterministic recurrent state $h_t$ (capturing long-term kinematic history) and a stochastic latent state $s_t$ (capturing transition uncertainty), maintaining belief across occlusions:
$$h_t = f_\theta(h_{t-1}, s_{t-1}, a_{t-1}), \quad s_t \sim p_\theta(s_t \mid h_t)$$

### Memory Domain Isolation

Embodied state estimation spans disparate time scales, demanding strict memory domain isolation across heterogeneous compute silicon.

```c
// STATIC PROPRIOCEPTIVE STATE BUFFER (MCU SRAM Domain 1)
// Zero dynamic heap allocation, deterministic compile-time memory layout
typedef struct {
    uint64_t timestamp_ptp_ns;
    float joint_positions[6];          // Radians (from optical encoders)
    float joint_velocities[6];         // Rad/s (differentiated in hardware)
    float motor_currents[6];           // Amperes (shunt resistor ADC readings)
    float winding_temps_c[6];          // Stator thermistor readings
    float imu_linear_accel[3];         // m/s^2 (SPI DMA transfer)
    float imu_angular_rates[3];        // rad/s
    uint32_t sequence_counter;
} mcu_proprioceptive_state_t;
```

| Memory Domain | Execution Substrate | State Representations | Update Rate | Memory Allocation | TTL Lease Horizon ($\tau_{\text{TTL}}$) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **Domain 1: Fast Proprioception** | Real-Time MCU (FreeRTOS / Bare Metal) | $q, \dot{q}, I_{\text{phase}}, T_{\text{motor}}, \mathbf{a}_{\text{imu}}, \boldsymbol{\omega}_{\text{imu}}$ | $1000\text{ Hz}$ | Static internal SRAM (Zero heap) | $5\text{ ms}$ |
| **Domain 2: Kinematic Frames** | Real-Time Linux MPU (`PREEMPT_RT`) | $T_B^A \in SE(3)$, Twist $\boldsymbol{\xi} \in \mathfrak{se}(3)$, `tf2` Tree | $200\text{ Hz}$ | Pinned Shared Memory (`mlockall`) | $20\text{ ms}$ |
| **Domain 3: Latent Semantic Belief** | Linux MPU + NPU / GPU Accelerator | JEPA $\mathbf{z}_t$, RSSM $h_t$, 3D Bounding Boxes | $10\text{--}30\text{ Hz}$ | DMA-mapped Unified DRAM (UMA) | $100\text{ ms}$ |

: Three-Tiered Memory Domain Isolation Architecture. High-level stochastic semantic representations (Domain 3) are strictly isolated from high-rate deterministic proprioception (Domain 1). {#tbl-memory-domains}

## Systems Failure Anatomy: The Stale Frame Tree Collision

The consequences of failing to correctly map state over time and coordinate frames manifest rapidly in hardware. 

![The 6-DoF Precision Articulated Manipulator Platform. Deployed in high-density surface-mount electronics assembly with wrist-mounted depth cameras and vacuum tooling. Fusing stale transform coordinates ($65\text{ ms}$ old) with real-time joint encoders without expanding spatial covariance caused a destructive collision with an aluminum fixture block.](figures/fig05_manipulator_arm_cropped.jpg){#fig-manipulator-arm width=100%}

**Platform:** 6-DoF Precision Articulated Manipulator ($v = 0.9\text{ m/s}$).

**Failure Mechanism:** During high-speed descent, the robot's mechanical forearm occluded the wrist camera for $180\text{ ms}$; the kinematics engine multiplied real-time joint encoders ($t_{\text{now}}$) with a stale camera transform ($t_{\text{now}} - 65\text{ ms}$).

**Root Cause:** Asynchronous coordinate frame multiplication across uncompensated sensor transport latency without expanding spatial covariance bounds ($\sigma_{\text{pos}}$).

Because the kinematic engine multiplied real-time joint angles ($t_{\text{now}}$) with an uncompensated stale camera transform from $t_{\text{now}} - 65\text{ ms}$, the computed target pose in the base frame was skewed by $0.9\text{ m/s} \times 0.065\text{ s} = 5.85\text{ cm}$. The arm descended into the solid aluminum fixture block, shattering the precision tooling.

| Timestamp | Subsystem & Substrate | Recorded State / Telemetry Event | Physical Implication |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **$T - 0.245\text{ s}$** | Wrist RGB-D Camera | Last valid visual detection of target PCB captured ($t_{\text{exp}} = 10\text{ ms}$). | Target coordinates valid in camera optical frame. |
| **$T - 0.180\text{ s}$** | Manipulator Forearm | Forearm linkage rotates into optical path, occluding PCB view for $180\text{ ms}$. | Zero new visual photons reach sensor die. |
| **$T - 0.065\text{ s}$** | Kinematic State Engine | Stale transform $\mathbf{T}_{\text{target}}^{\text{cam}}$ ($65\text{ ms}$ old) multiplied with $t_{\text{now}}$ joint encoders. | Frame tree multiplication injects $5.85\text{ cm}$ spatial skew. |
| **$T - 0.010\text{ s}$** | Trajectory Planner | Planner interpolates descent trajectory targeting corrupted base coordinates. | Gripper descends at $0.9\text{ m/s}$ toward solid metal fixture. |
| **$T + 0.000\text{ s}$** | Vacuum Gripper Tooling | Tooling strikes aluminum fixture block ($1.8\text{ kN}$ dynamic impact). | Tooling shatters; vacuum seals destroyed ($3,200\text{ USD}$ overhaul). |
| **Root Cause** | *Systems Bottleneck* | Asynchronous frame tree multiplication across uncompensated sensor transport latency ($65\text{ ms}$) without spatial covariance expansion. |
| **Architectural Flaw** | *Privilege & Co-Design* | Lack of time-indexed transform interpolation (`tf2` Lie algebra matching) and absence of hard Time-To-Live (TTL) state validity leases. |

: Flight-Recorder Telemetry Ledger: The Stale Frame Tree Collision Incident. Tracing uncompensated coordinate latency to mechanical tooling destruction. {#tbl-telemetry-ch05}


## The World State Belief Interface & Co-Design Checkpoint

To establish a deterministic boundary between temporal state estimation and downstream reasoning, the memory subsystem formalizes the **World State Belief Interface** (@tbl-dossier-state-belief):

| Parameter Category | Specification Key | Engineering Target Value | Verification Boundary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Root Coordinate Frame** | `frame_graph.root_frame` | `world` | Static Euclidean origin $[0, 0, 0]^T$ |
| **Kinematic Base Frame** | `frame_graph.base_frame` | `robot_base` | Rigid physical mounting base |
| **Transform Interpolation** | `transform_buffer.max_history_ms` | $500.0\text{ ms}$ | Continuous circular ring buffer |
| **Visual State TTL Lease** | `state_ttl_leases.visual_tracking_ttl_ms` | $100.0\text{ ms}$ | Revokes MPU proposal authority if $\Delta t > 100\text{ ms}$ |
| **Proprioceptive TTL Lease** | `state_ttl_leases.proprioceptive_ttl_ms` | $5.0\text{ ms}$ | MCU trips Category 2 safe stop if encoders drop |
| **Max Spatial Uncertainty** | `uncertainty_bounds.sigma_pos_max_mm` | $15.0\text{ mm}$ | Hard spatial confidence ceiling |
| **Anomaly Innovation Gate** | `anomaly_detection.mahalanobis_gate` | $3.0\sigma$ ($d_M \le 3.0$) | Rejects corrupt sensory detections / collisions |
| **Thermal Warning Knee** | `thermal_limits.warning_temp_c` | $85.0^\circ\text{C}$ | Initiates linear torque derating |
| **Thermal Emergency Cutoff** | `thermal_limits.critical_cutoff_c` | $105.0^\circ\text{C}$ | Immediate inverter bridge shutdown ($0\text{ Nm}$) |

### Systems Fallacies in Embodied State Modeling

::: {.callout-fallacy title="LLM Context Windows Substitute for Physical World Models"}
* **The Fallacy:** The internal latent representation or attention context window of a Multi-Modal LLM serves directly as an embodied world model.
* **The Physical Reality:** LLM context windows store token sequences, not metric spatial coordinates ($SE(3)$), Lie algebra velocity twists ($\mathfrak{se}(3)$), or physical mass distributions [@murray2017mathematical]. Autoregressive token generation lacks geometric invariance, metric scale calibration, and hard physical boundary enforcement.
:::

::: {.callout-fallacy title="Depth Cameras Deliver Metric Ground Truth Without Kinematic Tracking"}
* **The Fallacy:** A high-resolution depth camera provides ground-truth 3D coordinates without continuous extrinsic kinematic tracking.
* **The Physical Reality:** Camera mounting brackets flex and vibrate under mechanical robot accelerations ($>2g$). Without continuous extrinsic calibration tracking ($\mathbf{T}_{\text{camera}}^{\text{base}}$) and timestamp synchronization, static camera assumptions introduce centimeter-level metric grasp errors [@tobin2017domain; @peng2018sim].
:::

::: {.callout-fallacy title="Zero Process Noise Guarantees Kalman Filter Convergence"}
* **The Fallacy:** A Kalman filter will never diverge as long as process noise covariance $\mathbf{Q}$ is set to an arbitrarily small value.
* **The Physical Reality:** Setting process noise $\mathbf{Q}$ artificially small makes the estimator overconfident in its internal physical model. When real-world disturbances occur (such as wheel slip or external contact), an overconfident filter rejects valid sensory innovation updates ($\mathbf{y}_t$), causing the filter to diverge completely from physical reality [@thrun2005probabilistic].
:::

::: {.callout-fallacy title="State Estimation Belongs Entirely in User-Space Software"}
* **The Fallacy:** State estimation can execute entirely in user-space Python on the Linux application processor.
* **The Physical Reality:** If Linux experiences a background page fault, memory compaction stall, or kernel panic, user-space Python state estimation freezes. The bare-metal microcontroller must maintain an independent proprioceptive state estimator ($1000\text{ Hz}$) to compute dynamic stopping envelopes and execute safe hardware stops during MPU stalls.
:::

## Chapter Summary and Forward Handoff

This chapter established how embodied physical agents maintain structured spatial belief and temporal continuity across sensory occlusions. Physical state is not a stateless token sequence; it is a metric, dynamic $SE(3)$ coordinate tree integrated in Lie algebra tangent space ($\mathfrak{se}(3)$) and bounded by expanding uncertainty covariances.

By pairing latent world models (JEPAs, RSSMs) on the MPU with deterministic transform buffers and $1000\text{ Hz}$ proprioceptive state estimators on the MCU, we ensure that missing visual photons never induce open-loop physical destruction.

In the following chapter, **Chapter 6 (Reason: Expiring Intent Leases and Kinematic Affordances)**, we explore how physical agents reason about task goals, translate semantic instructions into bounded kinematic proposals, and enforce expiring intent leases before commanding multi-joint motion.
